quiz.q: According to Morton Kaplan, what defines the 'Unit Veto' model of international politics?
options: Every state possesses equal capability to destroy any adversary, making all actors equally powerful.
A single global superpower establishes a centralized hierarchical rule over all other nation-states.
A universal world government resolves interstate disputes through an overarching international legal authority.
Two dominant ideological superpowers maintain international stability by leading competing military alliances.
quiz.why: In Kaplan's unit veto model, every country has an equal capacity to destroy, giving each actor equal power.

quiz.q: In the Prisoner's Dilemma applied to international relations, why do states choose defection over mutual cooperation?
options: Leaders prioritize short-term domestic prestige over long-term strategic and economic security concerns.
Both states face a head-on collision where swerving first signals weakness and political surrender.
A severe trust deficit forces states to avoid the worst outcome rather than seek mutual benefit.
International institutions enforce binding sanctions that penalize countries attempting unilateral diplomatic restraint.
quiz.why: States cannot know rivals' intentions, so distrust leads them to defect to avoid the worst outcome.

quiz.q: How does the decision-making approach of Richard Snyder and colleagues conceptualize foreign policy formulation?
options: As a mechanical response to external systemic balances that strictly dictates national survival.
As a proactive process of identifying problems and selecting alternatives shaped by organizational and environmental factors.
As a reactive problem-solving exercise designed exclusively to handle acute military and diplomatic crises.
As an overarching grand theory that models recurring global interactions free from domestic influences.
quiz.why: Snyder views foreign policy as proactively discovering problems and alternatives, influenced by organizational and environmental settings.

quiz.q: Why did Stanley Hoffmann criticize Morton Kaplan's systems approach to international politics?
options: It relies excessively on game-theoretic zero-sum assumptions rather than empirical diplomatic history.
It focuses entirely on domestic decision-making processes while ignoring structural balance of power.
It overemphasizes post-colonial insecurity dilemmas at the expense of superpower alliance dynamics.
It reduces politics to an abstract parlour game, prioritizing rigid form over real political substance.
quiz.why: Hoffmann argued that systems theory reduces real politics to an unrealistic parlour game, elevating form over substance.
